issues: Integrity: no problems found. There is no file or network access and no pasted answers. Kernel weights and sigma2 are chosen by an inner GroupKFold over Murcko scaffolds on the training fold only. Test molecules only enter through K_te = tanimoto(test, train), which uses fingerprints, not labels.

Bugs: none that would make the result meaningless. A weighted sum of Tanimoto kernels with non-negative weights is still a valid kernel. The default best_cfg has length 4, which matches the 4 fingerprint sets, and the all-zero weight vector is skipped.

z: I could not reproduce the harness value exactly. Using a gain of 0.4968 - 0.4957 = 0.0011 and noise sd 0.0070 with 1 run vs 2, the standard error is 0.0070*sqrt(1 + 1/2) = 0.00857, so z ≈ 0.13. The harness reports 0.137, probably because it used a slightly different noise estimate. Either way the gain is far below noise.
No claims in the diff contradict the numbers. Rejecting is right: the gain is about 0.15 noise sd.

Not a veto issue: the inner grid of 80 weight vectors × 3 sigma2 values × 5 inner folds means about 1200 GP solves per outer fit. That costs a lot of runtime and adds code complexity, and choosing from that many options on ~780 training molecules risks overfitting the inner CV. The program card prefers simpler code when the gain is this small, which also supports rejecting.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff adds no file or network access and no pasted values. Test molecules are only passed through the LightGBM model to get leaf indices; their labels are never used.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. leaf_onehot uses width=31, which matches num_leaves=31, so the leaf indices (0 to 30) fit. The one-hot matrix is about 776 x 12400 floats, roughly 77 MB, well under the 6 GB limit.

Methodological caveat: the leaf kernel comes from a LightGBM model fitted to the same training targets, so choose_sigma2 picks the GP noise on a kernel that is already fitted to y. That may make the third component overconfident. It does not leak test labels or invalidate the score.
Minor cleanliness issue: W_DESC is no longer used in the return line, which is now an equal-weight 1/3 blend, so the constant is dead code. The new branch adds complexity with no gain.

Recomputed z: the candidate (0.4984) is 0.0016 worse than the incumbent mean (0.4968). The standard error is 0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00857, so z ≈ -0.187 (negative means worse). This matches the harness's -0.185 up to rounding of the means. The provisional reject is consistent with the numbers.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The new choice of the power p and the noise s2 uses only the training fold, through an inner GroupKFold split by Murcko scaffold. It reads no files and never touches test labels.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Raising a Tanimoto kernel to a power element by element keeps it a valid kernel (by the Schur product theorem). The same p is applied to both K_tr and K_te in the final prediction.
Small naming issue: choose_sigma2 now returns a pair (p, s2), so the name is out of date. This is cosmetic.
The inner search is now 9 settings instead of 3, so it costs about 3 times as much. The 10-minute limit was not hit.

My recomputed z is about -0.57 ((0.4968 - 0.5017) / (0.0070 * sqrt(1 + 1/2))). The harness reports -0.559, and the small gap is likely from rounding of the stored means. The candidate is slightly worse and the difference is within noise, so the decision to reject stands.
